newsitem.title: JAPAN: LSI Logic to ship single DVD chip in Q2 '97.
newsitem.headline: LSI Logic to ship single DVD chip in Q2 '97.

text.p: LSI Logic Corp of the United States said on Tuesday it would start shipments of a one-chip decoder designed specifically for digital video disc (DVD) players in Japan in the second quarter of 1997.
LSI chairman Wilfred Corrigan told a news conference in Tokyo that the growth of DVDs will provide it with a great business opportunity in the next few years.
"With its high resolution, high storage capacity and affordable price, DVD will truly have a profound impact on the digital electronics industry for years to come," he said.
He said LSI Logic's business focus is rapidly shifting to consumer products, such as set-top boxes for satellite broadcasting and video games, from the computer and communications markets.
The new single DVD chip will integrate nine separate chips, such as those for audio coding, on a single silicon chip.
A single chip will help to cut production costs for DVD makers, an LSI spokesman said.
Japanese sales will account for 30 percent of LSI Logic's global sales in 2000, up from the current 20 percent, Corrigan said.
